result.topic_en: Gauss defines two-variable theta-type series P(x,y), Q(x,y), R(x,y) and their values at y=1, then states duplication-type identities relating their squares and products to values at (xx,yy), including a derived identity for logarithmic derivatives in y.
result.transcription:
Es sei
$P(x,y) = 1 + x(y+\frac{1}{y}) + x^4(yy+\frac{1}{yy}) + x^9(y^3+\frac{1}{y^3})\ldots$
$Q(x,y) = P(-x,y)$
$R(x,y) = x^{\frac{1}{4}}(y^{\frac{1}{2}}+y^{-\frac{1}{2}}) + x^{\frac{9}{4}}(y^{\frac{3}{2}}+y^{-\frac{3}{2}}) + x^{\frac{25}{4}}(y^{\frac{5}{2}}+y^{-\frac{5}{2}})\ldots$
$Px = P(x,1),\ Qx = Q(x,1),\ Rx = R(x,1)$
Man hat dann
$P(x,y)^2 = Pxx.P(xx,yy) + Rxx.R(xx,yy)$
$Q(x,y)^2 = Pxx.P(xx.yy) - Rxx.R(xx,yy)$
$R(x,y)^2 = Rxx.P(xx,yy) - Pxx.R(xx,yy)$
I. $(Px)^2.P(x,y)^2 = (Qx)^2.Q(x,y)^2 + (Rx)^2.R(x,y)^2$ und indem die Differ. sich auf log y beziehen
$P(x,y)P''(x,y) - P'(x,y)^2 = P''xx.P(xx,yy) + R''xx.R(xx,yy)$
$P(x,y).Q(x,y) = Qxx.Q(xx,yy)$
$P(x,y).R(x,y) = Rx^{\frac{1}{2}}.R(x^{\frac{1}{2}},y^{\frac{1}{2}})$

methods.what: Definition of two-variable theta series P (theta_3-type), Q = P(-x,y) (theta_4-type), R (theta_2-type)
Theta constants as values at y=1
Duplication formula for square of P(x,y)
Duplication formula for square of Q(x,y)
Duplication formula for square of R(x,y)
Quartic-type theta relation between squares of theta functions with theta constants
Identity for second logarithmic derivative (derivatives w.r.t. log y) obtained by differentiating the duplication formula
Product formula P·Q in terms of Q at doubled arguments
Product formula P·R in terms of R at square-root arguments

items.english: One then has P(x,y)^2 = P(xx)·P(xx,yy) + R(xx)·R(xx,yy) (and the following identities).
